endorsements.quote: To enhance generalizability and clinical deployability, future studies should emph asize validation within unselected real -world screening cohorts, multi -center datasets, and geographically and temporally independent external populations.
Evaluations should also examine subgroup performance, batch effects, and cross -platform variability.

Adherence to established guidelines, including TRIPOD-AI, Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging, and Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP) will further strengthen transparency, reproducibility, and cross-study consistency111,112.
Beyond discriminative performance, model assessment must incorporate calibration to ensure reliable risk estimation.
Future research should adopt fixed feature sets, pre -specified analytical plans, transparent reporting, external benchmarking, and continuous real-world monitoring.

unlisted_practices: Prioritize multi-center data acquisition, standardized biospecimen processing, and matching or covariate adjustment for key confounders to mitigate data heterogeneity in AI model development.

Use domain adaptation, transfer learning, or domain-invariant representation learning to reduce cross-platform and cross-cohort distribution shifts, while not replacing prospective real-world validation.
Convene experts from government, industry, and academia to develop a consensus evaluation framework for AI models in medical settings.
Governments should set top-level regulatory frameworks defining acceptable development, validation, and clinical deployment of AI-assisted screening tools.
Consider private or hybrid deployments with end-to-end encryption to safeguard privacy and security of sensitive medical data.
Consider AI liability and errors-and-omissions insurance to mitigate legal and financial risks.

screen.reason: Commentary discussing the role, challenges (governance, bias, overdiagnosis), and future implementation of AI-empowered multi-cancer early detection.
